summary: The root جَسَسَ primarily means to feel or touch with the hand to ascertain something, often secretly or by exploring.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.gloss: He felt it with his hand; for the purpose of testing it, that he might form a judgment of it; The physician felt him

parts.t: He felt it with his hand
for the purpose of testing it, that he might form a judgment of it;
to know if he were hot or cold.
goat, to know if it were fat or lean.
is also, sometimes, with the eye. (IDrd, S, Msb. *) You say,

headwords.def: جَسَّهُ جس جسه جسة , (A, Mgh, K,*) or جَسَّهُ بِيَدِهِ , (S Msb,) aor جَسُسَ , (Mgh, Msb,) inf.n. جَسٌّ , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) He felt it with his hand (S, A, Mgh, K) for the purpose of testing it, that he might form a judgment of it; (Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ اجتسّهُ . (S, Msb, K.) You say, جَسَّهُ الطَّبِيبُ , (Mgh,) and جَسَّ يَدَهُ , (A,) The physician felt him, (Mgh,) and felt his arm, or hand, (A,) to know if he were hot or cold. (Mgh.) And جَسَّ الشَّاةَ He felt the sheep, or goat, to know if it were fat or lean. (A, Mgh.) جَسٌّ is also, sometimes, with the eye. (IDrd, S, Msb. *) You say, جَسَّهُ بِعَيْنِهِ (IDrd, S, A, K) (tropical:) He looked sharply, or intently, or attentively, at him, or it, for the purpose of investigation and clear perception.

headwords.def: مَجَسٌّ مجس (A, TA) and ↓ مَجَسَّةٌ (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) The place which one feels with his hand, (A,* Mgh, K, TA,) for the purpose of testing it, that he may form a judgment of it: (Mgh:) and ↓ the latter, the place which the physician feels [to know if a patient be hot or cold]: (S, Msb:) pl. مَجَاسُّ . (S, A, Msb, K.) You say, ↓ مَجَسَّتُهُ حَارَّةٌ [The place in which one feels him is hot]. (A, TA.) And كَيْفَ تَرَى مَجَسَّهَا [How dost thou find the place in which one feels her?]; referring to a sheep or goat; to which one answers, "Indicative of fatness." (A.) [Hence, (assumed tropical:) Anything external which indicates the internal condition. ] It is said in a prov., (S, A, Msb, K,) relating to camels, (Msb,)
